articles.title: Three things we learned as clueless Man United crash out of Carabao Cup after spectacularly bad performance

articles.body:
Manchester United were back in action tonight, taking on Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford in a Carabao Cup third-round fixture.

Following a poor performance in the 1-0 Manchester derby defeat, marred by a controversial VAR call over the Erling Haaland goal, United would certainly have been eager to get back on the pitch and deliver a top performance.

They certainly needed to silence the doubters by getting their act together and taking care of Brighton.

Unfortunately, they failed to do so, surrendering a two-goal lead (established by Shea Lacey and Mason Mount ) to lose 3-2 to a determined Brighton side.

There was plenty to unpack from this game. Here is what we learned:

Shea Lacey follows Rashford 's footsteps

Shea Lacey was handed his first Man United start, and he proved his worth. He rose to the occasion, breaking the deadlock with a beautiful strike from his left foot.

Injuries have been a nightmare for him, but promising performances like the one he produced against Brighton remind many why he is a top talent, an absolute joy to watch.

Lacey is now the first teenager to score on his first start for United since 18-year-old Marcus Rashford scored against FC Midtjylland in February 2016.

While the two are tipped to be the future of United's defence, this game showed they might not be ready to partner.

There were a lot of errors in their play, especially from Ayden Heaven . Leny Yoro looked decent and stayed alert to thwart danger, picking up where he left off against Sabah.

Heaven, however, had a rough night and was caught off guard in several situations. Had the young Englishman been alert before Charalampos Kostoulis's goal, he could have cut off the cross that the Greek striker converted.

Heaven's performance was concerning; sitting on the bench has, in a way, left him short of rhythm. More game time, perhaps partnering United's more experienced centre-backs, might help him find his feet.

Tielemans-Santos have not clicked as a pivot

The Youri Tielemans-Andrey Santos midfield once again struggled like it did versus Hull City. Their individual quality is there, but together the team lacks control, with zero movement and zero fluidity; they simply look static.

A Tielemans-Mainoo pivot has served Carrick well, while a Mount-Santos pairing has also shown promise. For now, Carrick would be wise to keep switching between the two before Carlos Baleba arrives and changes the dynamic.

That said, losing to the Seagulls and exiting the Carabao Cup was not the response expected after last weekend's derby disappointment.

It ought to serve as a clear wake-up call to the Red Devils that all is not well and that something must change before Sunday's clash with Fulham .

articles.title: A Manchester City debut years in the making should take place against Norwich City
articles.summary: Manchester City signed Gerónimo Rulli from Marseille this summer to be Gianluigi Donnarumma’s backup. James Trafford departed City for Leeds United, which me...
articles.body:
Manchester City signed Gerónimo Rulli from Marseille this summer to be Gianluigi Donnarumma 's backup. James Trafford departed City for Leeds United , which meant that City were in the market for another keeper. They decided to sign the experienced Argentinian keeper to fill an obvious hole in their squad. Enzo Maresca's side face Norwich City tomorrow night in the third round of the Carabao Cup at the Etihad Stadium. It is expected that Gerónimo Rulli will finally make his City debut in goal in a moment that has been years in the making.

If, as expected, Gerónimo Rulli starts in goal for Manchester City he will finally make his City debut.

Gerónimo Rulli returned to Manchester City this summer after having briefly been on City's books previously. Rulli was a City player during the 2016-17 season where he wss loaned out to Real Sociedad . He was eventually sold to the La Liga side without making a senior appearance for City. Given that City typically play their backup goalkeeper in the cup competitions it would seem that Rulli is in line to finally make his Manchester City debut against Norwich City. If that were to occur to would be a special moment for the Argentinian keeper.

Speaking with mancity.com , Gerónimo Rulli has revealed that by rejoining Manchester City this summer, he has fulfilled a significant career goal. Rulli said that wearing the City badge will be special moment for him. He explained: " I feel as though the circle has closed. I'm so happy to have achieved what I always wanted: to play for this club. Even before wearing the shirt, I felt part of me belonged at Manchester City. Wearing these colours and badge gives me a joy and emotion I hadn't felt in my career. "

It has been some journey for Gerónimo Rulli to finally be a permanent member of the City squad.

With the path that Gerónimo Rulli has taken throughout his career, he probably felt like he would never get the chance to play for Manchester City. The Argentinian keeper has played all over Europe since City sold him to Real Sociedad almost a decade ago. A return to City never really seemed likely for him. However, fate would have other ideas.

Manchester City needed an experienced goalkeeper to be Gianluigi Donnarumma's backup this season following James Trafford's departure. An opportunity for Rulli to come 'home' arose this summer. It was an opportunity that Rulli couldn't resist. City quickly wrapped up his signing from Marseille and now the experienced goalkeeper is a full-time member of Enzo Maresca's squad.

Gerónimo Rulli's story looks set to come full circle as he has a strong chance of making his Manchester City debut against Norwich City at the Etihad Stadium tomorrow night. If, as expected, that takes place, it will be special moment for him and one that has been years in the making.

Michigan basketball now knows its exact path to defending its national championship.

Big Ten Network hosted a special segment on Wednesday, Sept. 16, running through highlights from every league team's schedule before the Wolverines program announced the schedule in its entirety thereafter. Naturally, there are some highlights for the first season with coach Mike Boynton Jr. at the helm.

It starts in October, with a pair of interesting exhibitions; one against Oregon State (led by former U-M assistant coach Justin Joyner) and another against perennial power Houston, played in Grand Rapids. The non-conference also has a number of high-level matchups including a national championship rematch against UConn in Boston, a clash at home with Marquette, a game in Philadelphia against Villanova and another in Detroit against Louisville.

Michigan basketball 2026-27 roster for title defense

While Michigan leaves Ann Arbor for a number of games in its nonconference schedule, its first true road game doesn't come until its Big Ten opener against Rutgers in early December. From there, U-M only leaves Crisler Center once in the next month, when it goes to Nebraska in mid-January.

Later that month, Michigan has three out of four games on the road, traveling to Bloomington before its annual West Coast swing, this time with both Los Angeles-based schools in late January, before it returns home for the first of four rivalry matchups, hosting Ohio State.

Michigan will see MSU for the first time one day before Valentines Day, when Tom Izzo and the Spartans come to Ann Arbor on Feb. 13. That's the first of two meetings against the Spartans in a 13-day stretch − Michigan returns the trip to East Lansing on Feb. 26.

That's part of a difficult closing stretch, with four of Michigan's final six games on the road; at Minnesota, Penn State, MSU and then at Ohio State on senior day in Columbus.

The Big Ten Tournament begins the next week at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis; the Wolverines had great success there in 2024-25, winning the tournament the last time it was held in Indy in the first season under Dusty May.

A repeat will be a tall task, but Michigan is expected to be one of the better teams in the Big Ten. Its production is likely to come from its expected stars Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, added transfers Moustapha Thiam (Cincinnati), JP Estrella (Tennessee) and Jalen Reed (LSU), freshman McDonald's All-American Quinn Costello, and expected development from returners Quinn Costello and Ricky Liburd.

U-M will also likely find out this week if Roddy Gayle Jr. will be granted permission from the courts to return for a fifth season . The Wolverines also had a projected top-20 NBA Draft pick in freshman Brandon McCoy Jr., but he will be out for the season after he tore his ACL on the team's trip to Europe last month.

articles.title: New plans approved for Forest stadium expansion
articles.summary: The club is aiming to increase the City Ground's capacity to 52,500.
articles.body:
A major expansion of Nottingham Forest's stadium has been given the green light.

The club plans to increase the City Ground's capacity from 31,000 to 52,500 in two stages, at an estimated cost of £790m.

The proposals were approved by Rushcliffe Borough Council's planning committee on Wednesday.

Subject to a range of conditions, full planning permission has been granted to demolish and replace the Peter Taylor Stand and to redevelop the Trent End, which combined would take the ground's capacity to 45,000.

The club has also been granted outline planning permission to redevelop the Brian Clough Stand, which would add a further 7,500 seats.

The outline permission endorses the principle and scale of the latter, but final approval of more detailed designs will need to be given at a later date.

The plans also include a new public plaza and restaurant, as well as improved conferencing, media, and back-of-house facilities.

Forest were previously given permission to expand the ground to 35,000 seats under plans which were approved last summer , but unveiled more ambitious proposals a matter of months later which required fresh approval.

A spokesperson for the Nottingham Forest Supporters' Trust said: "On behalf of Forest supporters everywhere, we are delighted that our historic home has taken this major step to beginning its generational next chapter.

"We want to thank the club, our members, council officers and Rushcliffe Borough Planning Committee for their hard work getting us this far. It is a huge moment."

The latest plans have been backed by the city's MPs and the East Midlands mayor, Claire Ward.

"I see the expansion of the City Ground as the catalyst for what we could do across the Trent sports district," she said.

"This is a really unusual opportunity to have so many top flight sports so close to each other, whether that's the two football clubs, cricket, water sports, ice hockey, tennis, we've got so much going on in the city and I want this to be the starting point for that growth."

The MP for Rushcliffe, James Naish, said he was "delighted" the plans have been approved.

"It's something local people have been talking about for many many years and now we know the destination of travel which is fantastic," he said.

"Of course as the representative of the people of Rushcliffe I also care deeply about making sure local residents can live alongside the ground in as peaceful a way as possible, and that's why a lot of the conversations so far have been about parking."

As part of the plans, the club is set to pay more than £4m towards improvements to public transport and other infrastructure to encourage walking and cycling.

This includes a £990,000 contribution to proposed parking restrictions in the surrounding area, the details of which are yet to be confirmed.

Planning conditions state demolition work cannot begin, however, until a new plan is agreed to manage crowd flow on match days, which could involve building a new pedestrian and cycle bridge over the River Trent.

Nottinghamshire County Council and Nottingham City Council - which serve as the highways authorities for the area - have rejected a proposal to permanently close two traffic lanes on Trent Bridge.

Both councils say they otherwise support the stadium development.

articles.title: Michigan State basketball learns 2026-27 Big Ten schedule
articles.summary: Tom Izzo and Michigan State basketball now knows their 2026-27 Big Ten schedule to try and deliver Izzo a record 12th regular-season conference title.
articles.body:
The path to a Big Ten championship is set and will require Michigan State basketball to get through the defending national champs, with the hope that ultimately leads Tom Izzo back to Detroit and another Final Four.

The conference released its 2026-27 schedule Wednesday, Sept. 16. And Spartans know they will face Michigan twice, first in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Feb. 13 and then later in East Lansing on Friday, Feb. 26.

Izzo, who owns 11 regular season conference championships, will be looking to break a tie with Bob Knight and Ward "Piggy" Lambert for the most in Big Ten history. MSU won the Big Ten most recently in 2025 en route to an Elite Eight appearance.

The Spartans went 27-8 overall last season and made the Sweet 16 for third time in the past four years, finishing at 15-5 and in a three-way tie for second in Big Ten play after winning the league title the previous year. The postseason league tournament returns to Indianapolis from March 9–14.

The Wolverines and former coach Dusty May swept MSU last winter, 83-71 at Breslin Center and 90-80 at Crisler Center. U-M ran away with the Big Ten title and captured its first national title since 1989 in April.

Entering his 32nd season as the Spartans' head coach, Izzo is looking for his second national title to go with the one he won in 2000 and trying to get to his first Final Four since 2019, which was his eighth. MSU also is the host school for the 2027 Final Four at Ford Field on April 3 and 5 .

Along with playing defending Big Ten champ Michigan in the annual rivalry two-play, MSU will face Maryland and Nebraska both at Breslin Center and on the road.

The Spartans' home one-play opponents will be Minnesota, Oregon, Penn State, Purdue, Rutgers, Washington and Wisconsin. Their road-only games will be at Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Nebraska, Ohio State, UCLA and USC.

The games at USC and UCLA mark the second Los Angeles trip in three years since the Big Ten expanded to 18 teams in 2024-25. The Spartans will welcome Washington and Oregon after traveling to the Pacific Northwest last season.

Here is a look at MSU's schedule so far, with tip times TBD and a handful of nonconference dates still in the process of being finalized (*Big Ten games).

Nov. 26: Arkansas at Little Caesars Arena, Detroit

articles.title: ‘Put On a Good Show For Them’: Fever’s Sophie Cunningham Makes Her Feelings Clear on Getting Booed
articles.summary: Indiana Fever‘s Sophie Cunningham is having a very eventful season, and it is not just about how she plays on the court. She has been playing well, but she k...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever 's Sophie Cunningham is having a very eventful season, and it is not just about how she plays on the court. She has been playing well, but she keeps getting booed by fans at almost every game.

Cunningham has been part of many debates this season, and some of them started because of things she said publicly that people did not agree with. But the hate does not seem to bother her at all. In fact, she has said that she loves getting booed.

During the 2026 WNBA season, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham became one of the most polarizing figures in professional women's basketball.

On court, Cunningham has long played with an aggressive style brand of basketball. Throughout the season, she kept showing her tendency to engage in physical play and heated verbal exchanges such as a viral, animated confrontation where she pointed directly in the face of Connecticut Sun veteran DeWanna Bonner .

Beyond the court, she previously commented on biological males coming to WNBA. "I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men," Cunningham said about this issue. She was also involved in multiple on-the-court incident that makes the fans boo her almost in every game and every time she gets the ball.

Recently speaking with analyst Colin Cowherd, Cunningham has claimed that she does not mind getting booed, as a matter of fact she enjoys being hated. "It's so fun. When we're here at Gamebridge, it's so much fun because our fans are awesome, and you feel good leaving and (knowing) that you put on a good show for them," Cunningham said .

Sophie Cunningham acknowledged boos she gets when she plays in a different arena. Rather than pretending to be ignorant about it, she explained that she actually loves it. "But there is something special going into a different arena. Everyone knows it; I get booed 24/7. If I touch the ball, I get booed. The thing is, I f–king love that s–t. Bring it on."

Despite the public scrutiny, Sophie Cunningham is having a wonderful season with the Indiana Fevers.

Sophie Cunningham keeps doing her job amid public criticism

During the 2026 WNBA season, Sophie Cunningham played a crucial, high-energy role for the Indiana Fever as a primary reserve guard and bench spark plug. Returning on a one-year deal after recovering from a torn MCL sustained late in 2025, she carved out an impactful niche within Indiana's rotation.

Cunningham delivered one of the most efficient shooting years of her seven-year WNBA career. Averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists in about 22.7 minutes per game, her total scoring ended up comfortably above her career average of 7.9 points per contest.

Her biggest impact showed up in her efficiency numbers, where she set career highs by hitting 43.4% of her three-point attempts and 46.9% of her overall field goals, driving an elite True Shooting percentage near 66.9%.

Her steady bench production helped guide the Fever to a strong 26–14 regular-season record, securing a top postseason seed in the Eastern Conference heading into the playoffs.

articles.title: LeBron James Faces Polymarket Backlash as Fan Pulls Up Receipts on His Old Gambling Comments
articles.summary: LeBron James has spent years speaking openly about the growing place of gambling around sports. Now, a new business move has put those older comments back in...
articles.body:
LeBron James has spent years speaking openly about the growing place of gambling around sports. Now, a new business move has put those older comments back into the conversation.

James recently joined Polymarket, a prediction-market platform built around real-world events and outcomes. The timing is notable because James once questioned whether sports betting was taking some of the focus away from the games themselves.

LeBron James ' New Deal Brings His Old Comments Back

In 2023, James said that betting on sports makes the game less fair. He is worried that people care more about betting than about watching basketball.

A year later, James signed an endorsement deal with DraftKings. Now he has added Polymarket to that business portfolio, although the exact terms of his agreement with the company have not been disclosed.

The shift does not mean that James has changed his overall view of gambling. He has not stated that his previous criticism is no longer valid, and the information provided does not show a direct contradiction between his past comments and his current partnership.

What has changed is the setting. Polymarket deals in prediction markets, which puts James in a part of the betting conversation he once viewed with caution.

That alone would have been enough to attract attention. Then Kyrie Irving briefly entered the picture.

Kyrie Irving 's Repost Added A New Layer

The issue started when Eli Manning shared a post about Polymarket. A user named Nick replied, "I miss when there was a stigma to selling out." Irving briefly shared Nick's message before he took it down.

A screenshot of the repost was captured and shared by Omer Osman with the caption, "W repost, Kyrie Irving." The post did not remain online, and the available information does not establish that Irving was targeting James personally.

Still, the moment landed at an interesting time. James and Irving were already back in the public eye because of the 10-year anniversary of Cleveland 's 2016 championship, a reunion that Irving did not attend.

James had organized the gathering, while former teammates including J.R. Smith , Kevin Love and Tristan Thompson took part. Smith later said the group had tried to reach Irving, while Irving said he had prior commitments at the NBPA Top 100 Camp and called the coverage around his absence "psychotic."

That history helps explain why Irving's brief repost drew another look. But the more durable story sits with James himself.

His Polymarket partnership has reopened a question that James first raised when he criticized how betting was changing sports. The difference now is that he is no longer commenting from the outside.

articles.body:
The fallout surrounding the Kawhi Leonard saga has taken another turn. This time, the criticism is not coming from a rival player or another NBA team, but from one of the league's loudest television personalities.

Stephen A. Smith addressed the situation on Tuesday's edition of First Take . His argument centered on the gap between the punishment faced by the Clippers and what Leonard himself has had to deal with.

Kawhi Leonard Gets Put On Blast By Stephen A. Smith

Smith believes Leonard's role in the controversy cannot be separated from the consequences that followed. In his view, Leonard avoided the kind of personal fallout that eventually landed on the organization.

That is when Smith delivered his bluntest assessment of the situation.

"He's a gangster. I mean, to sit up there – he broke the rules, got caught, pointed the finger at somebody else, threw the organization under the bus, got his money and left the country," Smith said on First Take .

The accusation centers on Smith's reading of the events rather than on a new finding from the NBA. His criticism is that Leonard came through the controversy with his contract and playing status intact while the Clippers were left to absorb the major organizational penalties.

That contrast is what Smith appears to find most difficult to accept. He is not merely questioning the size of Leonard's punishment, but the overall outcome for the player compared with the franchise.

Kawhi Leonard's Outcome Has Stephen A. Talking

The NBA's decision led to a very different outcome for Leonard and the Clippers. Leonard was fined $700,000, while the Clippers received the far heavier penalties tied to the league's investigation.

Smith sees that imbalance as the most striking part of the story. He continued by arguing that Leonard's position after the investigation was hard to improve upon.

"I mean, how much better can it get than that? That is what Kawhi Leonard has done," Smith said.

That line captures Smith's broader complaint. Leonard was not suspended, his contract was not voided, and the Clippers carried the largest part of the punishment.

The criticism comes at a time when questions about Leonard's role in the Clippers controversy are still being discussed across the NBA. Smith has now put his own sharp label on that debate, arguing that the player benefited while the organization paid the heavier price.

For Leonard, the league's punishment remains on the record. So does Smith's very public assessment of how the entire episode played out.

articles.title: Deal agreed, midfielder set to return to Liverpool after four years
articles.summary: Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign a midfielder who left the club four years ago.Andoni Iraola has had a difficult start to life at Anfield. Most supporter...
articles.body:
Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign a midfielder who left the club four years ago.

Andoni Iraola has had a difficult start to life at Anfield. Most supporters will acknowledge that his job has not been made any easier by the squad he inherited.

It's a team that is very much all over the place in terms of balance.

Richard Hughes has left him with four wingers who prefer to play on the left side of the attack and none who prefer to play on the right.

Iraola also has just three senior midfield options, and none of them when playing together really fit into his philosophy. Trey Nyoni could offer that balance with Dominik Szoboszlai alongside him. However, Nyoni is young and inexperienced.

Liverpool's midfield solution is obvious

Having lost Curtis Jones in the summer window, there was an expectation that Liverpool would replace the academy graduate who departed for Inter Milan .

Ultimately, in the coming months that will need to change.

Liverpool can't do anything now until the January window. However, it's obvious that the profiles in the midfield need to change, that is the only way the Reds can solve their midfield conundrum.

And the perfect player is already out there. Lamine Camara was subject of interest from Liverpool and he continues to be monitored by the Reds.

January will present Liverpool with the perfect opportunity to bring the Senegalese international to Anfield.

Midfielder returns to Liverpool after four years

The Reds did sign a midfielder in the end. Liverpool have confirmed the arrival of Patrik Farkas, in an exciting move.

The Hungarian U19 international spent two years at the club between 2020 and 2022 playing alongside the likes of Keyrol Figueroa, Jayden Danns and Wellity Lucky.

Ultimately, he left Liverpool in 2022 to join Blackburn Rovers, where he came back to haunt the Reds scoring against Liverpool at U18 level.

However, he has now agreed a move to return to the Reds and his boyhood club after four years.

Farkas will join his younger brother Erik and three other Hungarians on the books including Dominik Szoboszlai, Milos Kerkez and Armin Pecsi.

articles.title: Red Sox Sit Jarren Duran, Shake Up Lineup For Rangers Matchup
articles.summary: The Red Sox removed Jarren Duran from Wednesday’s starting lineup and made several other changes before Game 2 against the Rangers.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox will give their lineup a significantly different look Wednesday night as they attempt to respond to a frustrating series-opening loss. Jarren Duran is out of the starting lineup against Texas Rangers left-hander MacKenzie Gore . Mickey Gasper and Nick Sogard also will begin the game on the bench after starting Tuesday's 4-2 defeat at Globe Life Field.

Jahmai Jones will replace Gasper at designated hitter and bat second. Isiah Kiner-Falefa enters at second base, while Nate Eaton will take over for Duran in center field.

Boston officially announced its revamped batting order on X before the second game of the three-game series. Roman Anthony remains in the leadoff spot and will play left field. Wilyer Abreu moves from fifth to third, while Willson Contreras stays in the cleanup spot.

Adley Rutschman drops two places in the order after batting third Tuesday. The catcher will hit fifth, followed by Caleb Durbin , Trevor Story , Kiner-Falefa and Eaton.

Jake Bennett will start on the mound for Boston. The left-hander enters Wednesday with a 9-7 record, a 3.69 ERA and 83 strikeouts. Gore will oppose Bennett for Texas. The Rangers left-hander is 8-11 with a 4.62 ERA and 172 strikeouts.

The matchup with Gore likely contributed to manager Chad Tracy loading the bottom half of his lineup with right-handed hitters. Jones, Contreras, Durbin, Story, Kiner-Falefa and Eaton all will bat from the right side. Boston needs a better collective offensive performance after producing only two runs in Tuesday's opener. Sogard supplied both with a two-run home run against Jacob deGrom in the third inning, but the Red Sox could not complete the comeback after falling behind 4-0.

The loss dropped Boston to 82-69 with only 11 regular-season games remaining. The Red Sox entered Wednesday 9 1/2 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East and 5 1/2 games behind the New York Yankees .

Wednesday's first pitch is scheduled for 8:05 p.m. ET at Globe Life Field. NESN will carry the game.

articles.title: Minnesota vs Akron Prediction: The Gophers Need To Rebound Fast
articles.summary: After an awful home loss, Minnesota must pick up the pieces with a big performance against Akron. Here's the CFN preview and prediction.
articles.body:
Minnesota (1-1) needs a short memory after an embarrassing 38-13 home loss to Mississippi State. Instead of last week being a showcase game for the Big Ten and PJ Fleck's Gophers, six wins and a bowl appearance are now in jeopardy, considering the brutal Big Ten season ahead. Akron (1-1) should be the opponent that makes things all better, but Joe Moorhead's team is plucky enough to make the Gophers fight. The Zips opened the season with a 38-16 loss to Wake Forest, but they weren't bad.

It's the first time the two teams have played each other. Minnesota usually doesn't crush MAC teams, beating Buffalo by 13 last year, Eastern Michigan 25-6 in 2023, and Miami University 31-26 in 2021.

The Gophers are on their way to Washington next week to start the Big Ten season, and then they host Michigan.

Akron gets a quirky home game against UNLV next week, and then starts the MAC campaign at Central Michigan.

Date: Saturday, September 19, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: BTN Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 3 Schedule, Picks – CFN Expert Picks: Week 3

Akron might not have a quarterback like Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor – who lit up the Gophers last week for three scores – but the Akron quarterbacks have been brilliant so far. The combination of Cibastian Broughton and Brayden Roggow completed 85% of their passes with six touchdowns and no picks. The Zips have the potential to dink and dunk Minnesota to death if the Gopher pass rush isn't generating any pressure.

Wake Forest lit up the Akron secondary like a Christmas tree. Gio Lopez and company hit the big plays, the little ones, and everything in between, getting up 38-3 before a few late Zip scores. Minnesota needs to take a deep breath and get Drake Lindsey going again. The Gopher star quarterback wasn't awful against Mississippi State, but he had a hard time getting anything moving deep. Akron doesn't have the pass rush to bother him.

This won't be a walk in the park if Minnesota pouts in any way after last week, but that's not how the program usually works under PJ Fleck. The Gophers will come out ready to play, but Akron really does have an efficient enough attack to keep this from getting out of hand.

articles.title: Painful endgame for Gray as stale Hibs slump
articles.summary: A club hero, David Gray ends his time as Hibs head coach not to the sound of euphoria from fans, but to the sound of a support collectively exhaling in relie...
articles.body:
It was the strangest kind of farewell; more sadness than satisfaction, more 'thanks for the memories' than 'never darken our door again'.

After a dozen years as a player, a goalscoring and Scottish Cup-winning icon, a coach, an interim manager and, for the last two-and-a-bit seasons, the first team manager, David Gray exited Hibernian on Wednesday evening.

He left, not to the sound of euphoria from the fans, but to the sound of a support collectively exhaling in relief. Given what he did on an immortal day at Hampden in 2016, no Hibs supporter wanted to boo the man they called Sir David Gray, nobody wanted to call for his head. It was a painful endgame, for everybody.

Hibs have sacked many managers in recent seasons, but this was no Nick Montgomery, no Lee Johnson, no Shaun Maloney. Gray was altogether different. Driven, passionate, honest as the day is long, brutally so when talking about how things were going wrong, which he had been doing too much of lately.

Gray's big picture tells us this: he was the first manager at Easter Road to qualify for European football in consecutive seasons since the great Eddie Turnbull in the early 1970s. The kind of slump that Hibs are in right now is entirely in keeping with what's happened at Hibs over the last half century.

He's the only Hibs manager to win at Ibrox in three consecutive seasons. He won at Celtic Park last season, too.

The flipside is also clear. Six successive home defeats in the league equals a grim club record dating back to 1920. Two shots at European Conference League play-offs - and the finance that would have come had they completed the task - were wasted in the most self-harming way.

Six points from six games, ninth in the table, an awful loss to lowly Kilmarnock on Tuesday and a sense of drift did for him. Making the League Cup semi-final, against Hearts, wasn't enough to save him.

The style of football wasn't easy on the eye, the lack of energy and entertainment was a problem that was only growing. Hibs just look a bit stale, a bit rudderless. Occasionally they can spark into life and show what they are capable of, but those moments have been too fleeting.

Jens Berthel Askou brought zest and enjoyment to Fir Park last season and Alfred Johansson, his successor, is trying to build on that. They both had bad nights on Tuesday but Johansson and Wouter Vrancken at Hearts are attempting to create something compelling and their fans are on board with them all the way.

Maybe Hibs fans want something similar, something shinier, something more exotic. There is the feeling that they have a decent enough squad of players but also a belief that these players should be delivering more than they are.

If there was a table for under-performance, Hibs would be challenging at the top.

Some of those same players must shoulder a chunk of the blame for Gray's demise, but they are a largely protected species, even if a number of them, weak-willed and unreliable, have no right to be protected. You can't sack a dressing room in one day, though. A manager and his assistants? Now that's different.

Gray goes but others must look in the mirror; the players, a sporting director in Malky Mackay, a chairman in Ian Gordon, a chief executive in Dan Barnett who could scarcely be more low-key if he lived in a bunker under Easter Road.

Gordon, presumably, will lead the search for another manager. It would be interesting to do a poll on the level of trust fans have in him and others to land the right man.

Gray took them to third in the league in his first season and fifth last season. There is an argument to be made that on the back of those bottom lines he deserved more time, but he hasn't got it.

He had a tumultuous beginning as Hibs manager; one league win in his first 14 games. In November he was bottom of the league. Hearts were second bottom. More than once Gray seemed to be in trouble only to pull out a series of wins that made him safe.

That first season was a prime example. From bottom of the table, he got them to third by the end. It was a fine achievement. Fifth last season was reasonable, but it must have felt nightmarish to Hibs fans as Hearts roared on and threatened to win the league.

The rise of Hearts adds significant pressure on whoever's managing Hibs. It's just the way it is.

Throughout his time, Hibs had a ruinous capacity to concede late goals that checked momentum and made the search for the holy grail of consistency all the harder.

In 2024-25 Hibs conceded late goals that cost them points against Kilmarnock, Ross County, Hearts, Dundee twice and Dundee United twice in minutes 88, 90, 90, 90, 86, 90, 87 and 90.

Last season that unfortunate habit of caving late on continued too often. They conceded damaging goals against Midtjylland, Legia Warsaw, Livingston, Dunfermline, Dundee and Hearts three times in minutes 119, 90, 98, 90, 90, 90, 88, 90 and 86.

This season they lost to Motherwell in the 85th minute and shipped goals in the 84th and 90th minute against Gent to exit the Conference League.

They salvaged a point, or three, on other days, but they were on the wrong side of the ledger on so many occasions. Gray will have regrets about that. What-might-have-beens. Plenty of 'if onlys' mark his time in the job. His players have cause for reflection, too.

They have no shortage of decent-to-good players at Hibs, but there is something missing, some steel, perhaps, some mentality, some leadership, some coaching nous.

Gray did his utmost to improve things. He always struck you as a manager who lived and breathed the job, who was terribly cut up by it when it didn't go to plan.

Most sacked managers think they could have improved things if they were given time. The betting is that Gray is one of those. He was in trouble in his first season and he found a way out of it to finish in a lofty position. He'd have backed himself to do the same in the months ahead, but that chance has gone now.

Hibs are back at the drawing board. Consistency there, at least. Meanwhile, Gray will start again somewhere else, hopefully strengthened by the experience of how brutal football management can be at times.
authors: Tom English - BBC Scotland's chief sports writer

articles.title: Guardians take back 1st place with 9 to play!
articles.summary: They're doing the thing again
articles.body:
The Ruberriest Rubber Match of them all! The White Sox and Guardians follow up Tuesday night's walk off with one final matchup this season (that is, if they don't face each other in the postseason) on Wednesday afternoon. Unfortunately for the Guardians, the season Tie-Breaker isn't up for grabs anymore, as Chicago secured that Monday night. However, 1st place in the division could finally switch hands for the first time since July 4th! So, would Cleveland take advantage of the recent momentum and reclaim 1st place? Or would Chicago take 2 in a series for the 4th of 4 matchups this season?

Going for Cleveland is Parker Messick , the steadiest arm in the Guardian rotation this season. Parker has had some solid success against the White Sox this year, throwing for 19.2 IP and only giving up 5 ER. That's good for a 2.28 ERA. The only problem with that is how he'd be up against. Did Chris Sale return to Chicago? Did Crochet or the ghost of Freddy Garcia?

Anthony Kay (L) would take the mound for Chicago, and if that doesn't annoy you, then you haven't been paying attention to the Cleveland Killing JAG of the year.

Kay in his 3 previous appearances vs Cleveland;

For those who aren't mathematicians, a guy with a career 4.90 ERA and just a 4.50 ERA this season came into this matchup with a 1.12 ERA over 16 Innings against Cleveland this year. To those who follow me on X, this isn't much of a surprise as I ~love~ to highlight the obscure Cleveland killers. Kay, to this point, has run away with the award for top Killer of the Year.

Through 2, both Parker and Anthony Kay were off to their typical starts (considering the opponent). It was in the 3rd inning when the Guardians broke through. Yes, some help was provided by the defense, but with 2 outs our new best bud Jo Adell came through with a 2 run single, putting the Guardians in front for the second day in a row.

Messick would run into a little trouble over the next two innings. And while he was able to work his way out of a bases loaded jam in the 4th, Tommy Pham would make him pay in the 5th, depositing a 3 run Homer into the bleachers.

So the Sox take the lead, everyone pouts, vents on Twitter and goes home in the 5th, right? Right?

What about these Guardians tells you to give up so quickly? I WOULD NEVER (I did, even as recently as last night) give up on them with so many outs to go!

And it's a good thing you don't either. Later in the 6th- with Anthony Kay already done for the day- Hagen Smith (L) came on for his second inning of relief work. He would get two outs but also walked two in the process, resulting in a pitching change, this time to a, you guessed it, Lefty in Sean Newcomb .

For what it's worth- Sean Newcomb was on my radar all winter as a legit LHRP option to slot between Sabrowski and Herrin on the depth chart. When the Sox got him I just knew he was gonna come up big this season. And right I was…

Newcomb came in with some obvious struggles. First 3 pitches wide before a get me over Fastball. And on the 3-1 pitch, known Slugger Petey Halpin launched one to the deepest part of the park for a 3 run Homer of his own, putting the Guards back on top.

The Guards would add on another after two 2-out walks and a double by Jose (still alive!), to take a 6-3 lead into the 7th inning. And with 86 pitches and a long layoff in the 6th, Steven Vogt decided to go from Parker Messick to, gulp, Hunter Gaddis .

Hunter might be leading the team in Love/Hate this season. While his numbers on the surface look solid, some have pointed out that it ~feels~ like he always struggles with the game on the line (last night was a prime example). And while to some extent I do agree that he unravels when we can LEAST afford it (first pitch swinging in every jam he's ever entered usually leads to a run or more, I have said), I also see him get the job done time and time again.

After 20 pitches last night, I was worried we might see a lawn chair out there today. But Gaddy held his own, giving up a double but nothing else. It was actually Erik Sabrowski that would run into some trouble with 2 walks in the 8th. Very frustrating since last night, it was the walks that did in the bullpen and I vented that the message to all relievers next year should be simple: "attack him, don't walk him" (as my semi-professional wrestler cousin told me last night- walks are like lost dogs; they always find their way home- and I kinda agree).

So with 2 on and 2 out in the 8th, Vogt treated today like he did yesterday: like a playoff game. Cade Smith was coming in for multiple innings of work. Would pinch hitter Sam Antonacci redeem last night's bad route to the final pitch?

Cade Smith would do his thing. Make quick work of all 4 batters securing his 37th Save of the season… and as my good friend Carrie would say, and just like that, like our lovely Samantha Jones, the Guardians would be back on top like they always are.

At 78-75, the Cleveland Guardians are, somehow, in 1st place in the AL Central with just 9 to play. But there's no time to rest- the Sox play tomorrow with a chance to tie for the lead, and with that tie breaker, would put us back a spot again.

The Guardians are off tomorrow before their final home series of the regular season this weekend, when they welcome the A's to town. The White Sox will be in Detroit for a 4 game series. Both teams will be off on Monday then 6 straight to end the season.

So buckle up, because it's a sprint to the finish line!

articles.title: Ryan Reaves Announces NHL Retirement After 16 Seasons, Played for Rangers, Penguins, Blues and More
articles.summary: Ryan Reaves is calling it a career.
articles.body:
The right winger announced on Instagram on Wednesday that he's retiring from the NHL after 16 seasons with seven different teams.

Reaves was drafted by the St. Louis Blues in the 2005 NHL draft and made his NHL debut with the team in 2010. After seven years with the Blues, he joined the Pittsburgh Pirates for the 2017-18 campaign but was traded to the Vegas Golden Knights halfway through the season.

He remained with the Golden Knights through the 2020-21 season, scoring a career-high 20 points during the 2018-19 campaign.

Reaves' time in Vegas ended in 2021 when he was traded to the New York Rangers, and he was then dealt to the Minnesota Wild during the 2022-23 season.

He signed with the Toronto Maple Leafs in free agency ahead of the 2023-24 season and ended his career with one year with the San Jose Sharks.

Reaves finishes his career with 962 games played, 66 goals and 74 assists. He'll be remembered for his physicality and fighting ability, which led to him spending 1,137 minutes in the penalty box.

"Today, I retire from the sport I've loved since I was 5 years old. It was a hell of a ride. Thank you to everyone who supported me throughout this journey. There are too many to single out, so you'll hear from me at some point," he wrote in his post.

"I may not be on the ice anymore, but I know I will always be close to hockey in one way or another. You can rest easy knowing the corners are a little safer today."

articles.title: Manchester United lose 3-2 to Brighton, crash out of League Cup
articles.summary: Brighton come from two goals down to win 3-2 at Old Trafford, to shock Manchester United as slow start continues.
articles.body:
Manchester United’s problems mounted as they crashed out of the League Cup after blowing a two-goal lead in a stunning 3-2 defeat against Brighton.

Michael Carrick’s side slumped to their second successive home defeat following a wretched collapse in the third round at Old Trafford.

United led through goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount inside just 10 minutes on Wednesday.

But Charalampos Kostoulas sparked Brighton’s revival and Pascal Gross equalised before Maxim De Cuyper grabbed the winner to leave Carrick shell-shocked as his team were booed off.

It was another brutal blow for United after their controversial 1-0 home defeat against Manchester City on Sunday.

The referees’ governing body admitted that VAR officials were wrong to allow City striker Erling Haaland’s winner, which left United with only one win from their first four Premier League matches.

Having led United to third place last season in his spell as interim boss, Carrick was expected to oversee a title challenge this term after being appointed on a permanent basis.

But United have already lost three of the six games in all competitions, putting Carrick under pressure to turn the tide at Fulham in the top-flight on Sunday.

A defeat in west London at the weekend would leave United in a full blown crisis barely a month into the new campaign.

Amid criticism of United’s close-season transfer recruitment, Carrick’s decision to make eight changes exposed the lack of depth in his squad.

At least Lacey offers hope for the future at United, unlike fellow highly-rated teenager JJ Gabriel, who has reportedly expressed his wish to leave Old Trafford.

The 19-year-old midfielder showed why Carrick has put his faith in him after eight minutes.

Taking possession just inside the Brighton penalty area, Lacey bagged his first ever goal for United as he lashed a clinical finish into the bottom corner.

Mount doubled United’s lead two minutes later, pouncing to fire into the roof of the net after Marcus Rashford’s shot was saved by Jason Steele.

But United’s defensive issues resurfaced in first half stoppage-time when Kostoulas punished poor marking from Ayden Heaven to drill past Karl Darlow.

That setback unnerved United and they conceded a 65th minute equaliser as Gross controlled Luka Vuskovic’s header and fired home from close-range.

Carrick’s men were in disarray and Brighton struck again in the 70th minute when De Cuyper swept Kostoulas’s pass into the net from six yards after sloppy United defending.

Carrick sent on Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha in the closing stages but United were unable to find an equaliser.

Brighton have now knocked United out of two cups in the space of nine months after winning in the FA Cup at Old Trafford in January.

It was the first time in 50 years that United had lost after being 2-0 up at home.

Tammy Abraham starred as Aston Villa won for just the second time this season, beating Coventry 3-1 at the CBS Arena.

Villa and Coventry are both in the Premier League relegation zone after dismal starts to the season.

Unai Emery’s men, beaten three times in four league games, showed signs of stopping the rot as Abraham slotted home from George Hemmings’s deft pass in the seventh minute.

Victor Torp hauled Coventry level with a superb free-kick in the 27th minute.

Ross Barkley restored Villa’s lead five minutes before half-time with a header from Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner.

Abraham killed off Coventry when he slotted home from Barkley’s flick in the 59th minute.

Charly Alcaraz came off the bench to seal Everton’s 1-0 win over second tier Wolves with a curling strike in the 80th minute.

Fourth tier Fleetwood Town reached the fourth round for the first time, beating Championship side Sheffield United 1-0.

On Tuesday, Arsenal won 4-2 at Ipswich, Liverpool beat troubled Tottenham 3-1, Fulham claimed a 3-2 win at West Ham and Brentford won 2-1 at Reading.

Holders Manchester City host Norwich on Thursday.

articles.title: Bears’ $110 Million Starter Suffers New Injury Before Vikings Game
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears held out one of their All-Pro starters with a new injury for their first practice for Week 2's matchup with the Vikings. The post Bears’ $1...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears had a new injury keep one of their All-Pro starters off the practice field on Wednesday as they began their preparation for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

The Bears officially added All-Pro right tackle Darnell Wright to their injury report and listed him as a non-participant following September 16's first practice of Week 2, raising concerns about the availability of their $110 million offensive lineman against the Vikings on Sunday.

Wright played all 75 offensive snaps for the Bears in their 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers and finished as Pro Football Focus' highest-graded overall offensive tackle (84.0) in Week 1, providing elite run-blocking to help pace Chicago to a league-leading 291 total rushing yards.

While Wright has two more practices to clear the injury report, his initial DNP in practice could pose a problem for the Bears as they prepare to face a blitz-happy Vikings defense under Brian Flores.

Theo Benedet is the backup right tackle on the Bears' depth chart and would be the likely candidate to replace Wright if he does not play against the Vikings, but their tackle depth is thin with Ozzy Trapilo still on the mend. Braxton Jones is currently starting in Trapilo's place at left tackle.

Bears Add Several Key Players to Week 2 Injury Report

Wright is the most significant new addition to the Bears' Week 2 injury report, but he is not their only notable contributor dealing with a new injury ahead of their matchup with the Vikings.

articles.title: Suburban League administrators seek split of OHSAA state tournaments
articles.summary: Could separate OHSAA public and private state tournaments be coming to Ohio? Suburban League administrators are pushing a petition to initiate that.
articles.body:
A petition led by administrators in the Suburban League could significantly change the landscape of future Ohio High School Athletic Association state tournaments.

A group of superintendents, principals and athletic directors in the Suburban League have organized a petition and are seeking a vote on whether the OHSAA should have separate public and private high school state tournaments.

The petition is circulating around the state, and the organizers have a December deadline to gather enough support in order to have a referendum item placed on the May 2027 ballot for high school principals.

Only high school principals can sign the petition. If organizers receive 75 signatures, including at least five from each of the six OHSAA districts, a petition would be placed on the May 2027 ballot for a vote from the full membership.

If a referendum passed in May, separate state tournaments could be implemented during the 2028-29 school year.

The issue was discussed at an OHSAA regional administrator update meeting on Tuesday, Sept. 8, at Streetsboro High School and on Tuesday, Sept. 15, at Princeton High School. These were the final two of six meetings to start the school year the OHSAA organized with administrators around the state.

There have been conversations over the years among OHSAA member schools about the potential separation of public and private high schools.

Petitions to separate state tournaments also took place in 1978 and 1993, but OHSAA member schools voted down each attempt.

Discussions to have separate state tournaments also took place in the late 2000s, leading to the formation of a competitive balance committee in 2010.

OHSAA member schools approved competitive balance in May 2014 and it was implemented ahead of the 2017-18 school year. OHSAA still uses it for the placement of schools into tournament divisions in the team sports of baseball, basketball, football, soccer, softball and volleyball. The modifications are based on which students are on a respective roster by sport at a high school.

The OHSAA's annual referendum voting period is from May 1-15 each year. Each member school has one vote to cast by the high school principal on each referendum issue on a ballot.

OHSAA Constitution Article 8-1-9 requires every member high school to submit a ballot.

OHSAA member schools passed 11 of 12 proposed revisions to the OHSAA Constitution and Bylaws in May 2026.

"At this point in time, we are going through the process as laid out by the OHSAA and their constitution and bylaws," Nordonia athletic director Rob Eckenrode said in a telephone conversation with the Beacon Journal on Tuesday, Sept. 15. "We have the referendum item ready to go, and as the bylaws call for we are soliciting signatures to get it on the ballot and see where it goes from there.

"… I think the item speaks for itself and we will see if we are able to secure the necessary number of signatures and then it would go up for a vote. Then it would be left up to all the schools in the state of Ohio to vote on it."

Eckenrode is in his 21styear as Nordonia's athletic director. He previously was an athletic director at Grafton Midview for four years and at Sullivan Black River for two years.

"We have a committee made up of athletic directors, principals and superintendents that have explored the possibility and have had multiple discussions about this and have met with the OHSAA to prepare the referendum item," Eckenrode said.

When asked if all 16 Suburban League schools have been involved in the petition, Eckenrode said: "Everyone is involved with the exception of Wadsworth. Wadsworth has specifically asked to not be included in the petition, in the referendum item and the process. I respect the folks at Wadsworth as a league member and they did not want to have their school's name associated with this."

The OHSAA is a voluntary, unincorporated and nonprofit membership organization that regulates interscholastic athletic competition for its member schools, consisting of 812 high schools (grades 9-12) and 741 seventh and eighth grade schools.

At the high school level, there are 691 public schools and 121 private schools competing in the OHSAA.

Other states with separate public and private state tournaments, according to the National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS), are Alabama, Maryland, Texas and Virginia.

With 347,994 high school student-athletes during the 2025-26 school year, Ohio ranked as the third-largest state for high school sports participation in the annual NFHS' Athletics Participation Survey, trailing only Texas (911,405) and California (859,022).

Following Ohio to round the top eight were Illinois (326,756), Pennsylvania (315,647), New York (312,563), Florida (311,233) and Michigan (295,634).

articles.body:
Wednesday afternoon, the Carolina Hurricanes officially released their roster and groupings for Training Camp, which begins Thursday morning.

The top group, 'C1', consists of eight defensemen, 14 forwards, and three goaltenders – and is primarily the usual crew we're used to seeing, as well as additional veteran defensemen.

Meanwhile, the second group, 'C2', consists of seven defensemen, 12 forwards, and three goaltenders – and is essentially the Chicago Wolves and young prospects wanting to make an impression.

A great sign is the presence of Seth Jarvis in the top group, just three months after undergoing shoulder surgery . Of course, it is anticipated that he will still miss the early portion of the season, but it seems that his recovery is coming along nicely.

Just last week, Jarvis also participated in a practice – even ripping a slap shot, as reported by WNCN's Todd Gibson.

On the flipside, Alexander Nikishin is not present due to his lack of a contract, as confirmed in a statement by general manager Eric Tulsky Wednesday.

This comes as little surprise, as a player just simply cannot participate in training camps and preseason without any form of contract – either of the full-fledged or of the professional try-out variety.

articles.title: Seahawks reveal uniform combo for Week 2 vs Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: Seattle will be bringing back their typical look against Arizona.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are gearing up for their first road game, and first divisional game, of the 2026 season this weekend. Seattle will be taking a trip to the Valley of the Sun to face the Arizona Cardinals , who are fresh off a shocking 1-0 upset victory over the Los Angeles Chargers .

We know this game will feature quarterback Drew Lock under center, as starter Sam Darnold has already been ruled out as expected. Now we know what Lock and the Seahawks will be wearing when they take the field this coming Sunday afternoon. On Wednesday, Seattle officially announced their Week 2 uniform combo. For the first time this year, the Seahawks will be pairing their navy home jersey with their grey pants.

Overall, the Seahawks are 9-7 in this particular combo, going 1-1 in them last year - including a win over the Arizona Cardinals . Seattle outlasted Arizona in a shocking 23-20 Thursday night thriller. The Cardinals clawed their way back from a 20-6 deficit to tie the game 20-20 with less than 30 seconds to go. However, Sam Darnold got the Seahawks in a position to walk it off with a 52-yard Jason Myers field goal.

The blue jersey/grey pants has been a typical combo when facing the Cardinals, having worn them in at least one of the two games against them for the past three seasons. Sunday will mark the fourth year in a row Seattle has worn this combo to play Arizona. As for the Cardinals, they will be wearing their funky desert-themed Nike Rivalries uniforms like they did in the aforementioned TNF game last year against Seattle.

articles.title: Patriots Get Positive Injury Update on 10-TD Scorer Amid A.J. Brown Absence
articles.summary: The New England Patriots will be without A.J. Brown for a couple of weeks, which is why this injury update on a key offensive playmaker is so important. The...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots did not put together the sort of performance they were hoping for in Week 1, as they suffered an ugly 13-10 loss at the hands of the Seattle Seahawks . Making matters even worse, star wide receiver A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve, meaning things are going to be tough for the Pats offense moving forward.

With Brown out, guys all over the board are going to have to step up. While all eyes will be on the wide receiver room, the rest of the offensive playmaker group will have to chip in, too. With that in mind, the team's latest injury update on running back TreVeyon Henderson will surely catch fans' attention.

TreVeyon Henderson Practices Fully for Patriots on Wednesday

A second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, Henderson overcame a slow start to the season for New England last year to become one of the more explosive offensive playmakers in the league. A threat to rip off a big play anytime he touches the football, Henderson racked up 911 yards and nine touchdowns on 180 carries, while also catching 35 passes for 221 yards and another score.

With Rhamondre Stevenson working alongside him, the Pats have one of the better one-two punches at running back when both guys are healthy and on the field. Late in training camp, though, Henderson suffered an ankle injury that led to him missing the team's Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.

Had Henderson played against Seattle, he could very well have made a difference in a close contest that saw New England in the lead for much of the action. Now that Brown is out, Henderson's status has become even more important, but in a positive development for the Patriots, he was able to log a full practice on Wednesday.

Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was a full participant in today's practice, an indication he could return on Sunday," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network shared in a post on X.

TreVeyon Henderson Tracking Towards Week 2 Return for Patriots

Henderson still has two days of practice to get through, but the fact that he was able to practice fully after not being able to take the field at all for a couple of weeks is quite encouraging. With Brown sidelined, you can make an argument that Henderson is the most dangerous playmaker at New England's disposal, meaning he will need to step up right away if he can play on Sunday.

Having Stevenson will allow the Patriots to ease Henderson into the action if he winds up being able to play, as the team won't want to risk having him reinjure his ankle. Henderson isn't out of the woods just yet, but if he keeps trending in the right direction, he will make his season debut in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The Diamondbacks reinstated right-handed pitcher Ryne Nelson from the 60-day injured list before their game on Wednesday, Sept. 16.

Nelson returns to the major league pitching staff after missing three months with a strained right elbow. He last pitched on June 15, earning a win against the Los Angeles Angels with seven innings of work.

Nelson made 15 starts this season, but he'll work out of the bullpen the rest of the season for Arizona .

"It feels really good to be back," Nelson said. "It's nice to get back here and hopefully contribute and push this thing in the right direction and do whatever I can to scratch some Ws out. It's been tough not being able to help but better late than never."

Nelson indicated he might not be using his full arsenal of pitches as a reliever. He said it was important to him to come back from injury and try to contribute, crediting the training staff at Salt River Fields for helping him.

Nelson was available for an inning-plus of work on Sept. 16 if called upon, Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said.

Right-handed pitcher Derek Law was designated for assignment, but the team encouraged Law to remain around the club in some capacity to stay prepared in case the Diamondbacks need a reliever for the postseason roster should they get there.

Patty Gasso and the Oklahoma Sooners softball team have earned their second commit of the 2028 class. In September, the Sooners have earned pledges from a top in-state recruit and the top overall arm in the country.

Sophia Schlader, the No. 1-ranked pitcher and the No. 3 overall player in the 2028 class, announced her commitment to the Sooners on Wednesday evening. A five-star prospect out of Urbandale, Iowa, she announced her decision at a ceremony at Waukee Northwest High School. Everyone in attendance and across the Red River watched to see if she'd pick Oklahoma or Texas - her final two schools being considered.

"Thank you, Coach Gasso, Coach JT (Gasso), Coach (Jennifer) Rocha, Coach (Falepolima) Steele and the entire OU staff for believing in me and giving me the opportunity to make a dream I've had since I was little come true," Schlader said in a social media post after the ceremony. "I couldn't be more excited to call Oklahoma home and can't wait for what's ahead! There's only one."

The 5-foot-8 right-handed pitcher and utility player is a 2025-26 Iowa Gatorade Player of the Year, a two-time state champion and one of the most dominant young pitchers in the country. As a sophomore at Waukee Northwest, she went 30-1 with 296 strikeouts in 187 innings. Ranked as the nation's No. 1 prospect in her class by Softball America, she also hit .357 with 29 RBI and 15 home runs, earning a spot on the Des Moines Register All-Iowa Elite Team.

"Her performance this season was outstanding from start to finish, both defensively and offensively," Des Moines Roosevelt High School head coach Christina Smith told Gatorade . "She was unstoppable at the state tournament and dominated in the circle. Outside of her performance, her leadership and the tone she sets for her team is fun to watch and is well respected."

Two weeks ago, Schlader took her visit to Oklahoma. Texas received her final visit just last week. But it was the Sooners that ultimately left the biggest impression. She's the 'Go Boomer' post from Gasso on Wednesday afternoon. The post featured a different spin this time, including a video from Sooner legends Jayda Coleman, Alyssa Britto, Kelly Maxwell, Ailana Agbayani, Alex Storako, Kinzie Hansen, Sam Landry, Tiare Jennings and Destinee Martinez, all welcoming Schlader to the program.

articles.title: Sports media reacts to FBS oversight committee admitting mistake in Michigan-WMU finish
articles.summary: The FBS oversight committee announced on Wednesday what anyone watching the Week 1 game between Michigan and Western Michigan already knew—the Broncos got ro...
articles.body:
The FBS oversight committee announced on Wednesday what anyone watching the Week 1 game between Michigan and Western Michigan already knew— the Broncos got robbed .

While the precise definition of "robbed" will vary from person to person—some called the phantom second added back onto the clock a conspiracy, while others simply noted what a weird sequence of events it was to allow Michigan an extra play —everyone watching at home was left confounded as Western Michigan shocked the world, only to be shocked right back .

In the immediate aftermath of the game, Western Michigan were first understanding of the outcome, but then later filed an appeal to the FBS oversight committee , arguing that proper clock protocols weren't followed in the final sequence of the game.

As it turns out, the FBS oversight committee agrees.

"The committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest's second-to-last play," the committee wrote in a statement . "Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different."

However, despite the acknowledgement that Western Michigan should have been named the rightful winner of the game, the statement also made clear that "the committee confirmed that it does not have the authority to overturn the contest."

This is a pretty comical turn of events, as it lands us in the worst of both worlds. Not only is it confirmed the wrong outcome was awarded, but also there is simply nothing that can be done to fix it.

Understandably, college football media was somewhat flummoxed by the statement.

So there you have it. The outcome of the game would have, and should have been different, but alas, nothing can be done, because the game has been declared final. Thus concludes one of the strangest moments in recent memory of one of our strangest sports.

Given how clearly the statement lays out that Michigan should have lost the game, it's possible that the selection committee will view the game as a loss , or something "loss-adjacent" let's say, should the Wolverines be in the postseason conversation later this year. That may provide Western Michigan a bit of cold comfort at least, but it does nothing to give back the high emotions that the Broncos should have been able to ride through the rest of the season based off of their performance against Michigan.

Everyone watching the game as it happened left confused, and despite not having an in-depth knowledge of the minutiae of end-of-game rule scenarios, it seemed the college football world was instantly in agreement of "that's not how that's supposed to work."

articles.title: Kentucky to get visit from elite 2027 shooting guard
articles.summary: As Kentucky basketball looks ahead to the 2027, they are setting up visits with top recruits, and will now host guard Adan Diggs.
articles.body:
Kentucky basketball coach Mark Pope had a breakthrough earlier this offseason by landing his first five-star recruit in Ryan Hampton. It's a great first addition to the 2027 class, but Pope is in the hunt for more, including guard Adan Diggs .

The Wildcats offered Diggs back in May, and have kept up communication with him, which led the guard to include Kentucky in his final seven last week. Now, per On3's Joe Tipton , Kentucky has set up a visit with Diggs as well, and will be in Lexington on Oct. 22-23.

Diggs is a 6'4", 180 lb combo guard out of Arizona. He is currently rated five stars by 247Sports and ranks as their No. 6 overall player in the 2027 class.

Arizona, being his home-state school, is the early favorite. However, Kentucky joined them in Diggs' final seven along with North Carolina , Arkansas, Kansas, Southern California , and the Duke Blue Devils , making a lot of elite competition for his services.

Adding a gifted scorer like Diggs would be a huge win for Pope. Diggs is an effective shooter, a good defender, and a terrific athlete. Getting him into Wildcats blue will be a priority, and they'll take their swing at him next month.

articles.title: Chris Drury, Mike Sullivan discuss exceptions for retooled Rangers heading into season
articles.summary: Coming off another disappointing season, Chris Drury knew that there were plenty of areas he needed to improve heading into the offseason -- months later, th...
articles.body:
Coming off another disappointing season, Chris Drury knew that there were plenty of areas he needed to improve heading into the offseason.

Months later, the Rangers ' GM feels he was able to check most of them off.

Speaking with reporters alongside head coach Mike Sullivan on the opening day of camp, Drury broke down how he feels about the roster heading in.

"We feel like we're in a good spot," Drury said. "A lot of changes, a lot of excitement, not just Ranger acquisitions but also with the prospects who are here trying to put their best foot forward -- I'm excited about what we've done."

With the additions and all of that rising young talent, Drury pointed directly towards the clubs depth as an area he feels they'll be better equipped throughout the year.

"When we were healthy last year our record was pretty good, when we weren't healthy it wasn't good," he said. "We just didn't have the depth to support missing those big pieces in the lineup, and when you lose those big pieces such as [ Adam ] Fox and [ Igor ] Shesterkin for chunks of time it's going hurt you."

Sullivan too expects that with that new and improved depth and some better luck on the injury-front, they'll be a more competitive group this year.

"We addressed some of the priorities we felt were important to help," he said. "At the end the day every team goes into camp with the goal that we're going to make the playoffs to give ourselves the opportunity for the Stanley Cup.

"My expectation is that we're going to compete -- we're going to be a competitive group with an expectation that we're going to compete every night and give ourselves a chance to make the playoffs and we'll see where it goes."

New York finished 34-39-9, and in the basement of the Eastern Conference in their first year under Sullivan.

articles.title: Patriots receivers say they're ready to step up with A.J. Brown on injured reserve
articles.summary: Drake Maye spent most of training camp this summer thinking about how the addition of wide receiver A.J. Brown could bring a new dynamic to the Patriots’ off...
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. (AP) — Drake Maye spent most of training camp this summer thinking about how the addition of wide receiver A.J. Brown could bring a new dynamic to the Patriots ' offense.

One game in, New England is adjusting to the reality of being without its top offseason acquisition for at least the next four games.

Brown left the Patriots' season-opening 13-10 loss to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks with a high ankle sprain that has since landed him on injured reserve.

It will certainly affect how the team prepares for games in the interim, beginning with Sunday's home opener against Pittsburgh . But coach Mike Vrabel doesn't believe his team's approach will change drastically.

"I don't think tweaked is really the answer. We're trying to install here and putting guys in spots that are best for them and best for us," Vrabel said. "We'll go through our game plan, and just like we did when A.J. was out there. ... We'll have to move guys around to different positions."

Those adjustments will put the onus on free agent pickup Romeo Doubs , along with the remaining group of receivers — Mack Hollins , DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams — who helped make up the core of Maye's pass-catching options during last season's Super Bowl run.

The performance of that foursome was a mixed bag in Week 1.

Doubs had a forgettable debut in which he didn't have a catch and dropped a wide-open pass late in the game that preceded Maye's third interception. That turnover set up Seattle's decisive field goal.

"Honestly, it happens to everybody," Williams said of Doubs. "We all know what type of player he is. It's all about brushing it off and worrying about what's up and coming."

Hollins and Douglas combined for nine catches for 71 yards against the Seahawks, while Williams wasn't targeted.

"Obviously, guys need to step up," Maye said. "They know that and they're ready for it."

Hollins ranked third on the team with 46 receptions and 550 yards last season and would seem likely to see an increase in targets.

One of Brown's biggest assets is that he can play multiple receiving positions. Vrabel said Hollins is equipped to do the same, is "always taking advantage of his opportunities" and has established himself as someone who will "be in the right spot when he's supposed to be there."

Douglas had 31 catches for 447 yards in 2025 and has shown his ability to be a deep threat for Maye.

The biggest unknown is what Williams could do with more targets. He had only 10 catches last season but averaged 20.9 yards per catch.

Williams said he's ready to take on an increased role and a chance to showcase his skills.

"I could give you a Christmas list for real," Williams said. "I could do a lot and just when the opportunity presents itself, I've got to show up."

articles.title: Madison Keys addresses pregnancy rumors started at 2026 US Open
articles.summary: On The Player's Box podcast, Madison Keys addressed the persistent pregnancy rumors circulating about her since her US Open loss to Qinwen Zheng.
articles.body:
Tennis fans were very concerned about Madison Keys after her third round US Open loss to Qinwen Zheng.

Zheng came from behind in dramatic fashion to win the match. An emotional and teary Keys said in her press conference that tennis was not fun. She also admitted changes were necessary.

Some fans thought that meant Keys was pregnant.

On The Player's Box podcast, Keys answered the pregnancy question

Keys, 31, said that she is not pregnant.

She also said if she was, it was no one's business.

Her emotions and demeanor were much better on The Player's Box podcast episode, co-hosted by Keys, Jessica Pegula, Jennifer Brady, and Desirae Krawczyk, that dropped on September 15. Keys had time to digest the tough loss.

Those who did not think she was hinting at pregnancy at that US Open press conference thought she may fire her coach. That could be problematic because she has been coached by her husband of nearly two years, Bjorn Fratangelo since 2023.

September 5, 2026; New York, United States; Madison Keys of the U.S. in action during her third round match against China's Qinwen Zheng. Mandatory Credit: Jerry Lai-Imagn Images

Fratangelo was instrumental in implementing a racquet change and serve adjustment after the 2024 season that directly resulted in Keys winning the 2025 Australian Open.

It seems unlikely she would fire her husband. Another alternative may be to add another person to her team to work with Fratangelo. These types of changes would not happen until the conclusion of the 2026 season .

In the meantime, Keys, ranked 23rd in the world, is preparing for the WTA 1000 China Open beginning September 30.

articles.title: Falcons news: Michael Penix Jr. on potentially returning from knee injury in Week 2
articles.summary: After the Atlanta Falcons’ disappointing Week 1 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, the fanbase has been concerned about the quarterback position after C...
articles.body:
After the Atlanta Falcons ' disappointing Week 1 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers , the fanbase has been concerned about the quarterback position after Cooper Rush started last Sunday. With Falcons star Michael Penix Jr. returning to practice , as he's still recovering from a partially torn ACL in Week 1 of last season, he would speak about the possibility of coming back on Sunday in Week 2 against the Carolina Panthers .

According to Marc Raimondi of ESPN, Penix would say that playing on Sunday is "still a possibility." Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Penix would emphasize how "close" he is to returning to the field.

"I know I've been saying that, but there's just a couple of technical things that I want to hit, some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do stuff out on that field. But I do feel really good, and we're taking strides each and every day," Penix said, via the team's website.

With Tagovailoa continuing to deal with an oblique injury and Rush throwing for 143 yards to go along with a touchdown and two interceptions, Penix would for sure be in contention as the starter, though there are "some goals" he wants to hit.

"I'm going to keep those to myself and the training staff, but I'm close," Penix continued. "Like I said, I'm close. I'm working extremely hard. I want to be out there. I'm dying to be out there. But at the same time, I've got to think about how I feel and think about things that I need to work on to make sure, you know, I hit before I go out there onto that football field."

At any rate, it remains to be seen if Penix will be ready for Week 2 or if it'll take more time.
