articles.title: Browns need to find their pass rush in Week 2 against Baker Mayfield
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns' defense, after a brutal Week One loss, must find its footing in the trenches against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns were completely overwhelmed in their 2026-27 NFL regular-season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars last Sunday.

On offense, veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson failed to consistently move the ball upfield for a majority of the contest. To make matters worse, head coach Todd Monken and the Browns could not establish themselves on the ground, as the offense tallied 87 rushing yards on 22 carries.

However, the most surprising takeaway from the Browns' season debut was the defensive struggles against quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the rest of the Jaguars' offense. The defense allowed 360 total offensive yards, while Lawrence accounted for 245 through the air and four touchdowns.

One of the key reasons for the lack of success on defense could have been the newest scheme from defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg. According to ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi, the Browns had blitzed Lawrence a total of three times on 21 dropbacks, which could have played a significant role in the Jaguars ' massive offensive performance.

Browns' defensive woes against the Jaguars

Despite losing star EDGE Myles Garrett , the Browns defense retained most of last season's playmakers. But Rutenberg's defensive scheme may have contributed to the slow start.

Throughout his time in Cleveland, former defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz was known for his heavy usage of man coverage, with the team playing 50 percent of the defensive snaps in zone coverage. On Sunday, however, the Browns played a total of 67 percent of their snaps in zone coverage, according to ESPN Research.

Still, the lack of man coverage should not be the main reason for the struggles on Sunday, as there are plenty of ways the defense could have used extra blitzers in zone coverage.

Last year, Rutenberg spent a season under the likes of Atlanta Falcons ' defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, who had the second-highest blitz rate at 33.9 percent, per Sharp Football Analysis . The lack of blitzes throughout the course of Sunday's contest was a surprise to many, given Rutenberg's background.

While the Browns' defensive playmakers knew the defensive scheme would change this year, Rutenberg must find creative ways to pressure the quarterback in Week Two against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Last week, the Cincinnati Bengals defense put plenty of pressure on quarterback Baker Mayfield , which led to a handful of mistakes.

For the Browns to win this week, the defense must step up on Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Dwyane Wade Jokes About His Forgotten Cavaliers Run With Brutally Funny 3-Month Admission
articles.summary: Former NBA star Dwyane Wade is synonymous with the Miami Heat. He’s often considered the greatest player in franchise history, based on his 15 seasons with t...
articles.body:
Former NBA star Dwyane Wade is synonymous with the Miami Heat . He's often considered the greatest player in franchise history, based on his 15 seasons with the team. However, some people often forget that Wade left the Heat for some time and played for two other organizations: the Chicago Bulls and Cleveland Cavaliers .

He left Miami to play for his hometown of Chicago in 2016. The following season, after a buyout from the Bulls, he signed with the Cavaliers to team up with former co-star LeBron James . However, his time in Cleveland was short-lived, and he played 46 games before they traded him to the Heat.

On Wednesday's episode of "Conversations With Cam Podcast," Wade joked about his stint with the Cavaliers.

"No one knows I played for Cleveland," Wade said . "They got me out of there. I was there for about 3 months and they said 'It's time for you to go homeboy'."

"No one knows I played for Cleveland," Wade said .

"They got me out of there. I was there for about 3 months and they said 'It's time for you to go homeboy'."

Initially, he left the team that drafted him because of the contract offer he received. The Heat gave him a two-year, $20 million contract in the 2016 offseason, while the Bulls offered him a two-year, $47 million deal. Aside from the money, it was a chance for Dwyane Wade to play for his hometown.

He played for the Bulls for a season and a half, averaging 18.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.8 assists. He shared the floor with Jimmy Butler and Rajon Rondo , lasting in the first round of the postseason . With the Cavaliers, however, he had a more limited role.

He appeared in fewer than 50 games and averaged 11.2 points, 3.9 rebounds and 3.5 assists. Wade played one more season after that before retiring from the league.

Richard Jefferson Claims Dwyane Wade Cost Him a Roster Spot

Before the Cavaliers traded for Dwyane Wade, former NBA player Richard Jefferson was still part of the roster. Jefferson, however, was dealt to the Atlanta Hawks in 2017 before ultimately being released. In a June episode of "The Richard Show," the one-time champion said Wade stole his roster spot.

"When D-Wade got bought out and he came. I'm looking around thinking, 'There's a roster problem here,'" Jefferson said . "And they're like, 'Yeah, Richard, we know.'"

Jefferson was part of the 2016 championship team and served as one of the veteran leaders in the locker room. Cleveland fans loved having him on the team. Despite spending just two seasons with the Cavaliers, he remained a fan favorite.

The current ESPN analyst averaged 5.6 points and 2.2 rebounds with the Cavaliers.

articles.title: Drew Doughty Named 15th Captain in Kings History After Anze Kopitar's NHL Retirement
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Kings announced Wednesday that defenseman Drew Doughty will be the 15th captain in team history following the retirement of Anze Kopitar, who wore the "C" for 10 years.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Kings announced Wednesday that defenseman Drew Doughty will be the 15th captain in team history following the retirement of Anze Kopitar, who wore the "C" for 10 years .

"Being named captain of an NHL team is something I'm truly honored by, and it's something I take great pride in," Doughty said in a statement . "I try to compete as hard as I possibly can every single day for this team, and winning is what fuels me, it's why I keep pushing to get better and chase success. The Kings mean everything to me. I've played my entire career here, and I want to lead this team by example, showing what it means to be a King and what it takes to win championships."

Doughty, 36, has spent his entire 18-year career with the Kings, which has included two Stanley Cup titles, five All-Star Game selections, and the Norris Trophy in the 2015-16 campaign.

His 1,279 games played in Los Angeles are just 17 shy of Dustin Brown for the second most in franchise history, and his 165 goals are the most scored by a defenseman in Kings' history.

"Drew Doughty has earned this," general manager and vice president Ken Holland said in a statement. "He's a champion who's won Stanley Cups and competed at the highest level of this game for a long time, and he's shown he can lead this team by the way he competes every day. That's the standard we want to set, and there's no one better to set it than Drew."

In the 2025-26 season Doughty appeared in 72 games and was plus-four on the year, notching five goals and 18 assists while averaging 23:05 of ice time per contest.

"Drew is a player I've admired from afar for a long time," head coach Peter Laviolette noted. "Since getting to know him better as a person, it's clear he's the right choice to be captain of this team. He sets the tone with the way he competes, and that's contagious."

Forwards Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin and defenseman Mikey Anderson will operate as alternate captains during the 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: Column: Fan angst at fever pitch as Cubs and White Sox take playoff hopes into final days of wild season
articles.summary: There have been few baseball seasons in Chicago like the one we’re going through. The Cubs and White Sox are fighting for a playoff spot with 11 days left, a...
articles.body:
There have been few baseball seasons in Chicago like the one we're going through.

The Cubs and White Sox are fighting for a playoff spot with 11 days left, and every game from here on out has meaning.

It could be an epic ending with both teams heading to the postseason for the first time in a full season since 2008. It could be a tragic ending with both falling short. Either way, it's probably going to make you shout at your TV, which is always a good thing.

Chicago is a great baseball town with a lot of baseball tradition but not a lot of hardware. So if you've been suffering from Cubs anxiety over the recent bullpen meltdowns or Sox sadness over all the sluggers' strikeouts, rest assured you are not alone.

The Sox lost 6-3 in Cleveland on Wednesday to fall out of first place for the first time since the Fourth of July after being one strike away Tuesday from taking the series and getting out of town on an up note. It was a classic Sox flip-flop, from ecstasy to agony in less than 24 hours. They have a 5-12 record since Aug. 30, when they were a season-high nine games over .500.

"I think we're in a good spot," manager Will Venable told reporters afterward, looking at the bright side of blowing the division lead after 2½ months.

The Cubs played the rubber game against the Atlanta Braves after blowing a late lead in Tuesday's loss and were neck-and-neck with the Philadelphia Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot heading into the weekend series in Cincinnati . They entered Wednesday with an 8-12 record since Aug. 25, when they were 20 games over .500. Manager Craig Counsell has been as optimistic as Venable, though it's hard to tell after a blown save.

Cubs and Sox fans are alternately dazed and confused, a rite of passage for most of them.

We're programmed at birth to hope for the best and prepare for the worst, no matter what side of town you grew up on. That's the legacy left by previous generations of Cubs and Sox fans, who've endured mostly the worst with a light sprinkling of the best.

As everyone knows, we've witnessed only two championships in our lifetimes and in our parents' lifetimes — and maybe even our grandparents' lifetimes. One is the loneliest number for fans of either team, and for Sox fans, it feels like a long time since 2005. Ditto for Cubs fans since 2016.

Sure, we deserve better. But as Clint Eastwood famously said in "The Unforgiven," "Deserve's got nothing to do with it."

The Cubs have a 99.5% chance to make the postseason, according to ESPN, so the biggest fear is they'll finish behind the Phillies or San Diego Padres and play the best-of-three wild-card series on the road.

At this point the Cubs might want to call up Justin Steele even if he's not ready, if only to steady the nerves of jittery fans. Most of them would rather see a hologram of Steele over most of the current members of the bullpen, which has 26 blown saves, including four in the first two weeks of September.

Cubs president of business operations Crane Kenney gave a pep talk at the daily ushers meeting before Wednesday's game, reminding them of how the home-field advantage worked so well in last year's wild-card win over the Padres. He was no Steele, but they seemed to appreciate the effort.

Pete Crow-Armstrong's MVP-caliber season wouldn't be complete without a playoff game at Wrigley, so the onus is on PCA and his teammate to make sure that happens.

The Sox had a 73.5% chance after Wednesday's loss, which suggests they'll still make it to October with a decent finish and some help. But they could also start out on the road, increasing the degree of difficulty.

There's still reason for optimism on the South Side, despite Colson Montgomery nearly striking out more in one season (211 times) than Hall of Fame second baseman Nellie Fox did over a 19-year career (216 times). The Sox still have the tiebreaker over the Guardians, so even though they're a half-game back in the American League Central, they can win out and clinch the division.

The Sox begin a four-game homestand Thursday against the suddenly competitive Detroit Tigers , who would like nothing better than to spoil the Sox season and make the magic wand irrelevant. It's also Tim Anderson Night, with the team honoring a former player who was considered the face of the franchise only five years ago before everything went downhill for the Sox.

Hopefully Sox fans will come out and honor Anderson and give the team a lift in the playoff race, despite the fact it's a school night. A half-filled Sox Park just doesn't cut it.

Venable told reporters after Wednesday's loss that even though the results in Cleveland weren't good, he was "proud" of the team.

The only news would be if Venable didn't say he was proud. But his incessant optimism is desperately needed right now as Sox fans try to process what's happening and wonder whether this wild, wild season would still be considered a success if they didn't make the postseason.

Former Sox catcher A.J. Pierzynski said on his "Foul Territory" podcast it would be an "organizational failure" if they did not after leading the division since July 4.

I'm not sure I buy that logic, since no one in the world had the Sox contending when they began spring training in February.

But it's true that general manager Chris Getz made several moves at the trade deadline, and none of them has panned out. Munetaka Murakami has virtually disappeared over the last two months, and Venable's handling of the pitching staff has been under fire. On the flip side, you could argue Venable got more out of this roster than any manager had a right to, and a .500 season would be about as good as anyone could've expected.

No matter what happens to the Cubs or Sox, it has been a fun summer in Chicago and full of memories that will last a lifetime.

Isn't that what watching sports is all about?

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Headlines Four AFC Quarterbacks the Rest of the Conference Cannot Stop
articles.summary: The Chiefs beat Denver, the Bills beat Houston 36-31, the Ravens dropped 41 on the Colts, and the Bengals won in Week 1 of the 2026 season. After a year in w...
articles.body:
The Chiefs beat Denver , the Bills beat Houston 36-31, the Ravens dropped 41 on the Colts , and the Bengals won in Week 1 of the 2026 season. After a year in which Kansas City missed the playoffs and Cincinnati struggled, the AFC's four marquee quarterbacks all opened with wins on the same weekend.

ESPN insider Adam Schefter pointed to those results as early confirmation of who will be running the conference race this season predicting four names the rest of the AFC will need to contend with.

Adam Schefter identifies AFC quarterbacks setting early championship standard

Schefter made the comments during his Week 1 breakdown naming Patrick Mahomes , Josh Allen , Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow . According to him, the AFC looked exactly like it has in its best years with the same names at the top and the same gap between them and everyone else.

"We got the Chiefs and Mahomes, the Bills and Allen, the Ravens and Lamar, and the Bengals and Joe Burrow. I'm just telling you. I see it already. It's one week, but it is not too early to say with those quarterbacks and those teams. We're going to be seeing those teams plenty of season. We're going to be talking about those teams plenty of the season," Schefter said .

Allen's win in Houston was something Schefter mentioned as worth noting. The Bills quarterback had lost four straight games in that building, including a prime-time loss last season, before throwing a go-ahead touchdown to Josh Palmer late in a 36-31 victory over one of the better defenses in the league.

"Who thought that Kenneth Walker would do that to Denver? Who thought Josh Allen would go into his own personal house of horrors in Houston where he had lost four games, where he hadn't won, where he got tormented on Thursday night last year, and light up arguably one of the best defenses in football," Schefter said. "I just keep coming back to this."

Kenneth Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown against Denver in Mahomes' return from injury, giving Kansas City a legitimate ground threat alongside its quarterback for the first time in years.

Chiefs and Bills back up Schefter's case with different kinds of wins

Josh Allen's win over Houston ended a major road problem, and Buffalo's 36-31 victory gave its quarterback an important response against a strong defense. Patrick Mahomes also gained a new run-game asset in Kenneth Walker, more weapons around him than he did a season ago, when the Chiefs finished 6-11 and missed the playoffs entirely.

Burrow and Cincinnati returning to the win column also matters. The Bengals were largely absent from the AFC conversation in 2025, and their Week 1 result put them back in the group Schefter is watching.

The Bills, Ravens, Chiefs and Bengals all have the roster depth and quarterback play to sustain early momentum. Jacksonville , Denver, Houston and the Chargers can still enter the picture, but one week of results already separated the contenders from the challengers in Schefter's view.

Whether those four teams are still standing in January is the only question that matters.

articles.title: Statler moves forward with plans for Josh Allen Gatorade banner
articles.summary: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) — Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen could soon make a reappearance on one of Buffalo’s most prominent buildings. The Statler building...
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) -- Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen could soon make a reappearance on one of Buffalo's most prominent buildings.

The Statler building is moving forward with its plans to put up a massive temporary banner featuring Allen. The planning board approved the variances at a meeting on Wednesday.

According to documents submitted to the city's zoning board of appeals, the banner will be about 110 feet by 120 feet.

A rendering shows a black and white photo of Allen and text that says "It Lives Here" with Gatorade and Bills logos.

The proposed banner would be up for about six months during the NFL season.

On Wednesday, an attorney representing the Statler went before the zoning board of appeals, requesting a variance for rules regarding the size of a sign, the length of time it's displayed and window obstruction rules. The variance for those requests was approved.

Fans may remember the popular Gatorade banner featuring Allen that was temporarily displayed in September 2024.

Patrick Ryan is an award-winning reporter who has been part of the News 4 team since 2020. See more of his work here and follow him on Twitter .

articles.title: Two Words From Patrick Mahomes to Chiefs Owner After His Return Are All Fans Needed to Hear
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has made his return to the field in the 2026 season and led his team to a dominant victory. The quarterback started and produced a great perf...
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes has made his return to the field in the 2026 season and led his team to a dominant victory. The quarterback started and produced a great performance as the Kansas City Chiefs recorded a huge 31-10 victory in their opening game of the season against the Denver Broncos .

It was also a special moment for Mahomes, who was out for a long time due to an injury sustained last season. A clip of him talking about his injury has become viral.

Viral clip shows Patrick Mahomes talking with Chiefs owner about injury

Mahomes was doubtful to start and play the opening game, but recovered in time. He missed the entire offseason training period for the Chiefs, after tearing the ACL and LCL in his left knee during a December 2025 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers . He underwent surgery the following day and spent the offseason rehabilitating.

In his first appearance since the injury against the Broncos, Mahomes completed 15 out of 27 attempts for 184 passing yards, two touchdowns, an interception and also recorded a rushing touchdown. He shared a special moment with his wife after the game.

After the final whistle, Yahoo Sports reporter Jori Epstein recorded a brief conversation between Mahomes and Chiefs co-owner Tavia Hunt. The two met after the game was over and shared a quick hug. Hunt asked him about his knee after missing so much time due to injury. In reply, the quarterback is heard saying, "I'm good. Glad to be back out there." The video of their interaction has since gone viral on social media, with fans talking about it.

It provides a reassuring update, as many feared the quarterback was rushing into action. It was previously thought that he would not be available for the Week 1 game, but he managed to surprise everyone. He did address that he was concerned about his injury during the game.

Patrick Mahomes admits feeling nervous during win against Broncos

In an interview with Sky Sports, Mahomes admitted that he was feeling nervous during the game. He said , "If I was going to say I was nervous for anything, it was getting hit on it. But I just wanted to play. I've done so much rehab and so much work to put myself in this position."

He added, "I just wanted to play. This is what you do it for. My guys around me helped me. I didn't play my best football and we went out and beat a really good football team pretty well, and it's because the guys around me stepped up."

Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will be celebrating their huge win, and focus on the next game.

articles.title: Three Major Takeaways from White Sox Series Loss to Cleveland
articles.summary: For the first time in 75 days, the Chicago White Sox will not be at the top of the American League Central Division. A 6-3 White Sox loss to the Cleveland Gu...
articles.body:
For the first time in 75 days, the Chicago White Sox will not be at the top of the American League Central Division. A 6-3 White Sox loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday caused them to drop the series against their division rivals. At this time two weeks ago, the South Siders had a 2 1/2 game lead over Cleveland, but today they are half a game behind them.

‎This is the first time since July that the Sox will have to chase from behind, and there are 10 games left to go in the regular season. However, the supercomputer MLB standings still favor the Sox to win the AL Central despite Wednesday's loss.

Three Takeaways from a Tough White Sox Loss

Anthony Kay had a 1.64 ERA across 16 innings against the Guardians before today's game. He had a good start on Wednesday, giving up two hits, two walks, and two unearned runs on a disastrous Chase Meidroth error. He threw 66 pitches before exiting in favor of Hagen Smith , who had a dominant fifth inning but collapsed in the sixth, allowing two walks.

‎Those two walks were the team's doom, even though manager Will Venable brought on Sean Newcomb for Smith. Newcomb immediately gave up a three-run home run to Petey Halpin , thus giving Cleveland the lead. He gave up two hits and two walks, contributing to a four-run inning. John Hicks and Noah Schultz finished up the game, with the White Sox already out of energy for a comeback.

Fans were caught by surprise after outfielder Tommy Pham was activated for Wednesday's game. Acquired at the end of August , he had told the team that he was ready to come back to the lineup. He was rewarded for his enthusiasm with DH duties and batting cleanup.

‎Many scoffed at the lineup, but Pham proved himself capable of the task in the fifth inning when he hit a three-run home run to give the White Sox a temporary 3-2 lead. Colson Montgomery and Tristan Peters were hitless, while Luisangel Acuña failed to come through with the bases loaded in the fourth inning.

‎ Rookie sensation Munetaka Murakami was benched today because of his hitless run . Since August 19, he has hit no home runs and accumulated 27 strikeouts.

After going down 6-3 in the sixth inning, the White Sox couldn't find their spark. And that has been obvious since the beginning of this month. White Sox fans knew that it would take everything the young team had after consecutive seasons of 100 losses , but didn't know it would come in September.

‎The team has been overburdened and has not been able to adjust to the battle-testing level of the major leagues. Roughly 20 players on the team roster are making their debut this season, which means they lack enough experience.

Nonetheless, they have had quite a season, way beyond anything White Sox fans expected. With the season winding down, the South Siders still have a shot to win their division and play in October. But no matter the outcome, the team has shown that it has what it takes to achieve big things in the near future.

articles.title: Raptors news: Darko Rajakovic reveals forgotten Kawhi Leonard NBA origin story
articles.summary: After the Toronto Raptors finalized their trade for Kawhi Leonard, head coach Darko Rajakovic revealed a story that the seven-time All-Star had never heard...
articles.body:
After the Toronto Raptors finalized their trade for Kawhi Leonard , head coach Darko Rajakovic revealed a story that the seven-time All-Star had never heard before. Upon Leonard's arrival, Rajakovic caught up with Kawhi in Toronto, where the two reconnected from their days with the San Antonio Spurs .

Rajakovic, who was an NBA scout ahead of Leonard's rookie season with the Spurs, talked about being present with the front office during the 2011 NBA Draft, where Kawhi was selected 15th overall by the Indiana Pacers before he was traded to San Antonio , he said, per Legion Hoops.

"I was working with San Antonio. I was coaching in Europe and I was their international scout," Rajakovic told Leonard. "So, the day you got drafted, I was with San Antonio in the draft room. I was part of the trade. I was like seven people. There was Lindsey, RC, coach Pop. I was there and a couple of scouts. And when we traded George Hill , and we got your draft rights, I was there when you got drafted."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Kawhi Leonard had no idea that Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic was alongside the Spurs' brass when they completed their trade with the Pacers.

"Wow, that's crazy," Leonard replied, which Rajakovic responded, "Small world."

Kawhi recalled seeing Rajakovic around the Spurs throughout his first season, but didn't know the former scout was in the team's war room during draft night.

"I remember seeing you around very vaguely," Leonard said. "Because Pop brings all the coaches over. So, I remember you a little bit, yeah."

Raptors' Leonard joins Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett as leaders who will look to build off their 4-3 first-round playoff exit against the Cleveland Cavs in 2026-27. Leonard, along with the 42nd overall pick ( Davis Bertans ), was traded to the Spurs in 2011 in exchange for George Hill, who was entering his fourth season.

articles.title: Cleveland Guardians Win White Sox Series And Climb Into 1st Place
articles.summary: With a bit more than a week to go in the 2026 Major League Baseball season, the Cleveland Guardians have moved into 1st place in the American League Central...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians moved into 1st place in the American League Central Division on Wednesday, September 16.

On a sunny afternoon, the Guardians won the rubber match of a crucial three game battle with the Chicago White Sox for first place, with a convincing, 6-3 victory.

The game was played if front of 23,336 fans at Progressive Field in Cleveland.

As mlb.com pointed out, the Guardians hadn't been in first place in the Central Division since they beat the same White Sox on July 4, 2026.

Left-handed rookie Parker Messick , who is having a fantastic season, gained the victory. Messick improved to .12-9 on the season, with a sparkling 2.57 ERA.

Cleveland Guardians Stars Of The Game On September 16:

1- Cleveland Guardians Petey Halpin - Centerfielder

There were plenty of accolades to go around following Cleveland's victory, but centerfielder Petey Halpin may get the largest bouquet.

It was Halpin's 3-run homer off White Sox reliever Sean Newcomb that turned the game and momentum around for Cleveland.

At the time the left-handed hitting Halpin, 24, stepped to the plate in the 5th inning, the Guardians were trailing the White Sox, 3-2.

It was the biggest single moment in rookie Halpin's young career.

Ironically, Guardians manager Stephen Vogt may have had designs on pinch-hitting for Halpin, as he may not have wanted the left-handed swinging Halpin to face the lefty, Newcomb.

But Vogt stuck with Halpin, and White Sox manager Will Venable stuck with Newcomb.

The Guardians went on to score a 4th run in the inning, and Messick and three relievers shut down the explosive White Sox the rest of the game.

2- Cleveland Guardians Parker Messick-Starting Pitcher

cbssports .com notes that Messick now has 14 quality starts for the season.

A quality start occurs when a starting pitcher goes at least 6 innings, yielding 3 or less runs.

For example, in his last six starts, covering a total of 36 innings, Messick has yielded 10 earned runs, has struck out 44, and has won four of the six games.

Messick pitches with a quick pace, and uses his tremendous rhythm to keep focused.

As noted by brooksbasesball.net, Messick uses a very complete repertoire of a four-seam fastball, a sinker, a slider, a changeup, a cutter, and a curveball in his arsenal.

Messick has a knack for keeping the hitter off balance, and changing his eye level.

Messick has helped a Cleveland Guardians rotation that may have been showing some signs of fatigues recently.

The Guardians bullpen has been a strength of the club all season.

In the game September 16, these three relievers came in and shut down the powerful White Sox bats:

Evan Gaddis-RHP=1 inning, 1 hit, no runs

Eric Sabrowski-LHP-0.2 inning, no hits, no runs, two walks

Cade Smith -RHP (closer) 1.1 innings, no hits, no runs, two strikeouts

Smith earned his 37th save in the game. He trails only the Tampa Bay Rays Bryan Baker for the most American League saves.

4- Cleveland Guardians Jose Ramirez -Third Baseman

Cleveland Guardians icon, Jose Ramirez has been negatively impacted in his game by lingering pain from hamate bone surgery.

Ramirez has been hitting and playing in pain, and his impact on the offense has been minimal.

Ramirez had two loud, ringing doubles, one of which drove in a run.

If Ramirez gets his swing back, and impacts a baseball as he did September 16, the Guardians will have a major weapon back on offense.

5- Cleveland Guardians Jo Adell -Right Fielder

Adell had a big base hit to drive in two runs in the game.

Since arriving in Cleveland in a trade with the Los Angeles Angels , Adell has hit nine doubles, and six home runs. He has driven in 28 runs.

Adell has provided the Guardians with much needed power from the right side of the plate, which had been missing most of the season.

Adell has played outstanding defense in both right and left fields, and his contributions to the Guardians 1st place position in the American League Central must not be denied.

Conclusions About Cleveland Guardians September 16 First Place Victory:

The Cleveland Guardians bats may have awakened.

The Cleveland Guardians now hold sole possession of 1st place in the American League Central Division. A true team effort, with lots of stars contributing, paved the way for that lofty position on a tough victory against the Chicago White Sox on September 16.

I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans," a statement from Boehly said.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."

None of this will do much to dispel the rumours that there was a serious rift between Boehly and Clearlake head Behdad Eghbali, which surfaced in 2024. Fans can hope that a unified ownership will be able to perform better than what we've seen in the last 4 and a half years.

Xabi Alonso has more players likely to be available on Friday night – but there are long term consequences for picking them.

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck Suspended by Jets After Trade Request, Latest NHL Rumors on 3-Time Vezina Winner
articles.summary: The saga between Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets continued on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The saga between Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets continued on Wednesday.

The three-time Vezina Award winner did not report to camp after publicly requesting a trade in August, and he'll now be suspended by the team. He reportedly informed the team that he wouldn't attend camp.

After the Jets' dissapointing 2025-26 campaign, speculation began to arise about whether Hellebuyck would ask out in hopes of joining a contender as he seeks his first championship.

Hellebuyck addressed the speculation in August when he released a statement saying that he had requested a trade.

"Several months ago, I privately requested a trade. I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options," Hellebuyck wrote in a statement released by his agent. "With training camp approaching, I felt it was important to publicly confirm my request. My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family."

Jets general manager Kevin Chevaldayoff followed with a statement that said the team would "continue to work through the situation in a thoughtful manner."

Several weeks later, there has been no resolution, and now it appears tension could be building between the two sides.

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported before the NHL draft that the Jets were believed to be in talks with the Buffalo Sabres about a deal for Hellebuyck, but those trade discussions seemingly fizzled.

The team reportedly is seeking a goalie to replace Hellebuyck and is focusing on immediate help rather than future picks, but it might be difficult to get that kind of return for him.

While Hellebuyck is an accomplished goalie and one of the best of his generation, he's 33 years old and is owed $8.7 million in cap space per year over the next five seasons. Even if he's still playing at a high level, it's hard to say whether he will be for years to come.

Hellebuyck and the Jets are clearly at an impasse, and whether they'll find a solution before the start of the season remains to be seen.

articles.title: From the corner, Avinash Sable returns to the spotlight at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Fewer athletes will carry greater expectations for India at the Asian Games than Avinash Sable.The defending Asian Games champion, Asian Games record .
articles.body: Fewer athletes will carry greater expectations for India at the Asian Games than Avinash Sable.The defending Asian Games champion, Asian Games record holder (8:19.50) and national record holder (8:09.91) in 3000m steeplechase heads to the continental showpiece as one of the country’s most dependable gold-medal prospects.For much of the last year, however, the possibility of Sable defending his steeplechase crown looked far from certain as he suffered a horrific crash during water jump at Monaco Diamond League in July 2025. It caused severe ACL and meniscus tears in his right knee.The injury turned even routine training into a challenge and forced the 31-year-old through months of rehabilitation before he could begin preparing seriously for another championship campaign.“It’s not a small story,” coach Kalyan Chaudhuri told TOI in an exclusive interview.“After the ACL tear, even jogging was difficult. The last seven to eight months were very crucial. The actual preparation started only around three or four months ago because rebuilding strength for hurdling, water jumps and race-specific work was not easy.”Now, with the Games approaching, Chaudhuri believes Sable has recovered sufficiently to challenge for another steeplechase gold while also contesting the 5000m, in which he won a silver in Hangzhou.His recent performance at the Indian Athletics Series Final in New Delhi last week where he won the men’s 3000m steeplechase title with a timing of 8:32.39 was also encouraging.But the comeback has not been without setbacks.During a high-altitude camp in Ooty in April this year, Sable suffered a thigh strain that interrupted his progress and required another round of rehabilitation. According to Chaudhuri, the period between May and mid-June proved decisive in accelerating his recovery.“We focussed on strengthening, particularly around the knee, after the ACL repair. That phase was crucial in regaining his previous strength and endurance,” said the deputy chief national athletics coach.While the ACL injury has not affected Sable’s hurdling or water-jump technique, Chaudhuri admitted there are still subtle reminders of the setback during training.According to the coach, his running mechanics can occasionally appear slightly altered during warm-ups and slower-paced movement before settling into their natural rhythm. Once he moves into race-specific sessions, however, he “runs absolutely fine like before”.The coach credited a larger support system involving recovery specialists, strength and conditioning experts and SAI Bengaluru staff for helping Sable return to elite competition. Yet he believes the athlete’s own understanding of his body has played an equally important role.“He is one of the most intelligent athletes I have worked with. He knows the response of his body and understands what is required for recovery. Training such an intelligent athlete is really a blessing for a coach,” Chaudhuri said.While competition opportunities have been limited since the injury, the signs have been promising. Sable clocked 13:45.52 in a 5000m race in Belgium last month and has subsequently posted encouraging performances in training.The coach conceded that serious injuries can sometimes leave lingering doubts in an athlete’s mind, particularly in a crowded steeplechase race where competitors jostle for position approaching barriers and water jumps. However, he says Sable remains mentally unfazed.“My feeling is that after such an injury there can be a little fear in crowded situations, but he tells me he is completely used to it now. He says he feels no difference,” Chaudhuri added.Beyond his medal ambitions, Sable has also emerged as a mentor within India’s middle and long-distance running set-up. But after a year spent battling injury, rehabilitation and uncertainty, the defending champion will now be just focussed on himself as he takes another shot at continental glory.If Chaudhuri’s assessment is accurate, Sable could once again find himself at the forefront of India’s athletics campaign in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, chasing the kind of performance that has defined his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brewers' nightmare seeding, matchup scenarios for 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have already completed their first objective by clinching a fourth consecutive National League Central title. Their remaining games are...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers have already completed their first objective by clinching a fourth consecutive National League Central title. Their remaining games are not ceremonial. Milwaukee still needs to secure the postseason route most likely to keep its historic season alive.

The Brewers head into Thursday at 95-57, three games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the National League's best record. They also own the head-to-head tiebreaker against the Dodgers after winning four of seven meetings. The Atlanta Braves lead the NL East at 89-64 and sit another three and a half games behind L.A.

This positioning gives Milwaukee control of the No. 1 seed with 10 games remaining. Surrendering it would create the team's most dangerous realistic bracket.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

If the current standings hold, the top-seeded Brewers would face the winner of a Wild Card Series between the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies . The No. 2 seed would draw the winner between the Braves and the San Diego Padres . Neither route offers an easy opponent, but the second path carries considerably more risk.

The Padres represent Milwaukee's worst individual matchup. San Diego took four of the six meetings between the two clubs this season, including a three-game sweep at Petco Park in August. The Brewers entered that series with baseball's best record and left without a victory. San Diego has also surged toward October, winning nine of its last 10 games through Wednesday.

A drop to the No. 2 seed could therefore reward the Brewers with an NLDS against the opponent that gave them the most trouble. The Braves would hardly offer relief . Atlanta is 89-64 with a plus-111 run differential and enough postseason experience to punish any team in a short series.

Holding onto the No. 1 overall seed in the NL would keep the Braves and Padres on the opposite side of the bracket, but it would not eliminate every nightmare scenario.

The Phillies are the most dangerous opponent on the Brewers' current path. Philadelphia is 84-68 and has played better away from Citizens Bank Park, posting an impressive 43-34 record away from home. Kyle Schwarber leads the majors with 45 home runs, while Bryce Harper and Trea Turner give the Phillies several hitters capable of changing a game with one swing.

The Brewers won two of three against the Phillies in June, but their season series remains unfinished. The teams will meet three more times at Citizens Bank Park from September 22-24. Those games will provide a potential NLDS preview and give the Brewers an immediate opportunity to test themselves against the opponent they should least want emerging from the Wild Card round.

The ideal matchup is the Cubs. Chicago has scored 817 runs and features another dangerous lineup, but the Brewers went 9-4 against their division rival. The Brewers won five of their final seven meetings, including a three-game September sweep at American Family Field. Familiarity, recent success, and home-field advantage would make the Cubs the most favorable option .

Milwaukee is equipped to beat any of these teams. Jacob Misiorowski is 15-5 with a 1.89 ERA, while Logan Henderson owns a 10-3 record and 2.51 ERA through 17 starts. The Brewers have also outscored opponents by 200 runs.

That strength should create confidence, not indifference. A five-game series leaves little time to overcome a poor matchup.

The clearest route is retaining the No. 1 seed, avoiding the Braves-Padres side and drawing the Cubs. If the Phillies advance, it would complicate that path. Falling behind the Dodgers could make it significantly worse.

The Brewers have built the National League's best record. Their final task is ensuring the bracket rewards them.
